extracted.intended_audience: ICML 2022 reviewers (peer reviewers for an ML conference)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing submissions to the ICML 2022 conference: procedural responsibilities (onboarding, bidding, conflicts, deadlines), how to evaluate papers across core aspects, how to write constructive, evidence-backed reviews, and how to participate in rebuttal/discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle of reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing should create value for the authors by giving them actionable feedback to potentially improve their papers; and for the community by helping authors improve their papers and helping with the decisions to publish papers that advance our field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be professional and constructive. Unprofessional reviews can harm authors and the community. Reviewers are expected to follow the ICML 2022 ethics guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onboarding and conflict disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept the invitation in CMT and provide the information for CMT that will help the paper assignment (TPMS, google scholar id, subject areas, etc.). Indicate possible conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete profile information promptly so meta-reviewers can assign papers appropriately. Flag conflicts as soon as they are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding and expertise flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Bid on papers. Once papers are assigned, flag any conflicts by communicating with the meta-reviewers. Also flag if a paper lies too far from your expertise to the degree that it will be hard to provide a good review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do this quickly so meta-reviewers can find alternate reviewers; be explicit when a paper is outside your expertise rather than providing a low-quality review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and meeting deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit reviews in time and keep track of the deadlines. Any delays increase the load on your colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to meet Phase 1 and Phase 2 deadlines; late reviews disrupt assignment and discussion phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in rebuttal and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the rebuttal and modify your reviews if necessary. Reviewers and meta-reviewers should discuss contradictions if any between the reviews, and between the reviews and the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively participate in discussion phase; update your assessment based on author clarifications and peer discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin by reading the review form and planning aspects to evaluate
rubrics_metrics.description: Before starting to review a paper, read the review form and think about the aspects of the paper that need to be evaluated: (1) Novelty, relevance, significance, (2) Soundness, (3) Quality of writing/presentation, (4) Literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a list of the contributions claimed in the paper for yourself; structure your reading with these aspects in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, relevance and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer: In what way does the paper advance our field? Whether there are, or you can imagine, readers in the community who could plausibly benefit from reading the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate overall ideas, techniques and results rather than focusing on a single aspect. High novelty/significance in one area may be sufficient. Consider plausible beneficiaries/readers in the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness (technical correctness and supporting evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check carefully the support for the contributions you identified. Each of them needs to be checked individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify proofs, derivations, experiments, and claims. Distinguish between unsupported claims and those backed by sufficient evidence; explain deficiencies specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer: Is the paper effective in explaining the contributions it makes? If not, how could it be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out unclear explanations, missing definitions, poor organization, or presentation issues; suggest concrete improvements authors can implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature and contextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the paper places the research presented into the context of current research. Papers cannot expect to cite other papers made public within a month before submission; such recent papers should be considered concurrent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use judgement for citing unpublished/preprint work according to subfield norms; if an omitted relevant publication would not change conclusions, treat omission as a minor issue; consult meta-reviewer if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of a good review
rubrics_metrics.description: First write the summary of contributions; follow by filling out each individual aspect evaluating it on its own; finish by summarizing strengths and potential weaknesses, ranking them by importance for acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the summary clear and accurate; ensure each review-form aspect is addressed separately and that the final recommendation is tied to the ranked strengths/weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify concerns as major or minor
rubrics_metrics.description: The review must clearly classify any concern mentioned as either a major or a minor concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major concern is one that either invalidates one or more main contributions of the paper, or one that requires extensive changes to the paper and as such the revision would need to be re-reviewed. Trivial issues that don't affect conclusions are minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation dimensions (primary bases for decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper is evaluated solely based on its relevance, soundness, novelty, completeness and the quality of writing/presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus assessment and scoring on these dimensions and avoid extraneous criteria (e.g., author's affiliation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive, specific concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The review should focus on the research in a constructive manner. The concerns raised are specific with enough details so that the authors can act on them, and they are informative for the meta-reviewer, senior meta-reviewer and program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable feedback (what to change, where), not vague criticism. Explain why an issue matters and how it affects conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and describe strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: The review identifies the strengths of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list positive aspects (novel ideas, clear experiments, useful insights) to give balanced feedback and help meta-reviewers and authors understand value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and correctness of claims in the review
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims that the review makes are precise enough and correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating or misrepresenting the paper; back up assertions with quotes, pointers, or evidence from the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence backing review claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims that the review makes are backed up by evidence, and the evidence provided in the review is sufficient to understand the claims made in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific experiments, figures, equations, page/line numbers when pointing out problems or strengths so others can verify your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbered comments for author rebuttal reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If a list of comments is used, the comments are numbered so that the authors can refer to them in their rebuttal if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numbered lists for discrete issues to make the rebuttal and discussion easier and more precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear references to parts of the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Any references to parts of the paper are clearly identifiable (e.g., page/line numbers given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing where an issue appears, give exact locations so authors and meta-reviewers can locate them quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable improvement suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors will find it easy to understand how the review suggests improvements to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete guidance (rewrite this paragraph, add baseline X, include sensitivity analysis) rather than only pointing out problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient detail for meta-reviewer decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The meta-reviewer will find the review detailed enough to help them make a decision. In particular, limitations of the review are clearly identified in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State if some analyses were infeasible to check, if experiments could not be reproduced, or if the reviewer lacks expertise in some sub-aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: The spelling and grammar in the review are checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread the review; poor language undermines clarity and professionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness and professional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The language of the review is polite, respectful, kind and professional (avoid any personal comments, e.g., do NOT write 'Authors fail..' but write 'The work fails to..').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid personal attacks, keep tone neutral and focused on the work. Be especially mindful of how criticism affects students and junior authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for biases and objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Double check for your own biases and objectivity. Did you adhere to the very first sentence of this tutorial?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on potential conflicts, affiliation biases, or methodological preferences that might skew your judgment; aim for fair assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow paper-writing best practices and critical commentary etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews (and the evaluation of papers) should adhere to the expectations mentioned in the paper writing best practices document and to norms such as Daniel Dennett’s points about composing criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dennett-style advice: re-express the authors' position clearly and fairly, list points of agreement, mention anything learned from the paper, and only then offer rebuttal/criticism. This order improves fairness and clarity.
